content.text: Original project-authored synthetic reference v1. A simplified enclosed milling cell with a spindle, table and coolant loop. All numeric values and observations are invented for this educational fixture and must not configure real equipment. Review authorized lockout/tagout and verification of stored-energy isolation before physical access. Use correlated observations and compare competing causes. In this authored fixture, increased tool overhang and the controlled comparison support insufficient tooling stiffness. Vibration alone would not distinguish this from bearings or workholding.

content.title: A change in surface finish
content.briefing: A milling cell develops a rough finish after a tooling change. Production is paused in the training record. Investigate the evidence before proposing a cause.
hints: Compare at least two independent observations before selecting a diagnosis.
A reading outside its training range is evidence, but does not establish a cause by itself.
steps: Review the simulated safety plan: authorized lockout/tagout, stored-energy isolation and verification before physical access.
Inspect the recorded visual evidence. This simulation does not authorize access to real machinery.
Read the archived condition measurements and compare them with this fixture's training envelope.
Compare the recorded operating history with a competing explanation.
Review the virtual verification evidence, then justify a diagnosis using the strongest observations.

evidence.label: Tooling record
evidence.text: The recorded tool assembly has greater overhang than the stable comparison setup.

evidence.label: Controlled comparison
evidence.text: In the archived virtual comparison, shorter overhang reduces vibration at the same simulated cutting conditions.

evidence.label: Coolant record
evidence.text: Flow remains within the synthetic range; the recorded workpiece receives coolant.

evidence.label: Maintenance history
evidence.text: No change in the recorded bearing trend preceded the tool change.

content.explanation: In this authored fixture, increased tool overhang and the controlled comparison support insufficient tooling stiffness. Vibration alone would not distinguish this from bearings or workholding.
rationale_rubric: 0–10: connects the two distinguishing observations to the proposed cause; partial credit for a supported but incomplete link.
0–10: compares one credible alternative and explains what evidence weakens it; no credit for unsupported certainty.
